facts.statement: Chinshakiangosaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Chinshakiangosaurus (JIN-shah-jiahng-uh-SOR-us, meaning "Chinshakiang lizard") is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: The body length of the only known specimen is estimated at 12 to 13 meters.
facts.quote: The body length of the only specimen is estimated at 12 to 13 meters.

facts.statement: The dentary was curved in dorsal view, forming a U-shaped, broad snout typical of sauropods.
facts.quote: The dentary was curved in dorsal view, so that the mandibles formed a U-shaped, broad snout.

facts.statement: There were 19 teeth on each side of the mandible, more than in any known sauropod but fewer than in the prosauropod Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: On each side of the mandible there were 19 teeth – more than in all known sauropods, but fewer than in the prosauropod Plateosaurus.

facts.statement: A prominent diagonal ridge on the dentary suggests the presence of fleshy cheeks, a feature previously only known from prosauropods.
facts.quote: In lateral view, the dentary shows a prominent ridge running diagonally across the bone. Apart from Chinshakiangosaurus, this feature is only known from prosauropods, where it is interpreted as the insertion point of a fleshy cheek.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in 1970 by Zhao Xijin and colleagues in Yongren County, central Yunnan.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in 1970 by Zhao Xijin and colleagues in Yongren County in central Yunnan.

facts.statement: The fossils come from the Fengjiahe Formation, composed of mudstones, siltstones, and sandstones deposited in river and lake environments.
facts.quote: They come from the Fengjiahe Formation, which is made up of mudstones, siltstones and sandstones that were deposited fluviolacustrine (inside rivers and lakes).

facts.statement: Associated invertebrate fossils suggest an Upper Jurassic age, though a more precise date could not be determined.
facts.quote: Fossils of invertebrates like ostracodes and bivalves were used to determine these sediments as Upper Jurassic in age. A more precise dating could not be made.

facts.statement: C. H. Ye named the specimen Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis in 1975, after the Yangtze River and the village of Zhonghe.
facts.quote: C. H. Ye mentioned this specimen in 1975 under the name Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis (after the Yangtze River and the village Zhonghe).

facts.statement: The name remained invalid as a nomen nudum until Dong Zhiming published a description in 1992.
facts.quote: However, because he did not provide a description of the fossils, the name was a nomen nudum (nacked name) until Dong Zhiming published a short description in 1992.

facts.statement: Upchurch and colleagues declared Chinshakiangosaurus a valid taxon in 2007 after a comprehensive description of the dentary and teeth.
facts.quote: In 2007, Upchurch and colleagues published a comprehensive description of the dentary and the teeth and declared Chinshakiangosaurus as a valid taxon.

facts.statement: Dong Zhiming initially classified Chinshakiangosaurus as a member of the prosauropod group Melanorosauridae.
facts.quote: Initially, Dong Zhiming classified Chinshakiangosaurus as a member of the Melanorosauridae, which he thought to be a group of prosauropods.

facts.statement: Recent studies classify Chinshakiangosaurus as a very basal sauropod.
facts.quote: More recent studies classify this genus as a very basal sauropod.

facts.statement: Chinshakiangosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Jurassic,

facts.statement: It lived approximately 185 million years ago during the Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico inferior, hace aproximadamente 185 millones de años, en el Toarciano, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the broad snout of Chinshakiangosaurus indicates it was a bulk feeder adapted to consume large amounts of foliage, unlike selective feeders with tapered snouts.
facts.quote: Paul Upchurch and colleagues (2007) suppose that this differences can give hints about feeding habits: The prosauropods with their tapered snouts possibly where selective feeders, who ate only certain plant parts, whereas sauropods with their broad snouts where bulk feeders, adapted to consume large amounts of foliage.

facts.statement: A bony plate lining the tooth row likely prevented teeth displacement while stripping plants.
facts.quote: This plate may have hindered the teeth to be displaced while defoliating plants.

facts.statement: Fleshy cheeks would have prevented food from falling out of the mouth and may indicate some degree of oral processing before swallowing.
facts.quote: Such cheeks would have prohibited food falling out of the mouth and may be a hint that the food underwent some degree of oral processing before it was swallowed.

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic relationships of Chinshakiangosaurus remain unclear.
facts.quote: The exact relationships are not clear, though.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Chinshakiangosaurus is a valid taxon, with some earlier studies classifying it as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2007, Upchurch and colleagues published a comprehensive description of the dentary and the teeth and declared Chinshakiangosaurus as a valid taxon.

facts.statement: Fossils were recovered from the Dianzhong lowlands in China in 1970 by Zhao Xijin and colleagues in the county of Yongren.
facts.quote: Los restos de Chinshakiangosaurus fueron recobrados de los bajíos de Dianzhong, China en 1970 por Zhao Xijin y sus colegas en el condado de Yongren.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Ye in 1975, but a formal description was not published until Dong Zhiming did so in 1992.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado por Ye en 1975, pero no se realizó una descripción, hasta que Dong Zhiming lo hiciese en 1992.

facts.statement: Invertebrate fossils such as ostracods and bivalves helped determine that the sediments containing the remains are from the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de invertebrados como ostracodos y bivalvos se utilizaron para determinar estos sedimentos como del Jurásico superior.

facts.statement: Known remains include the lower jaw, some vertebrae, scapulae, hip bones, and hind limb bones.
facts.quote: Se conocen la mandíbula inferior, algunas vértebras, escápula, huesos de la cadera y de las patas traseras.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V14474 consists of a left dentary, one cervical vertebra, several dorsal and caudal vertebrae, both scapulae, some pelvic bones, and hind limb bones.
facts.quote: El espécimen de holotipo, IVPP V14474 consiste en un dentario izquierdo, un cervical y varias vértebras dorsales y caudales, ambas escápulas, algunos huesos de la pelvis y las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: Ye named the specimen Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis in 1975, referencing the Yangtze River and the town of Zhonghe.
facts.quote: Ye mencionó este espécimen en 1975 bajo el nombre de Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis por el río Yangtze y el pueblo Zhonghe.

facts.statement: Upchurch and colleagues mentioned the genus in 2004, classifying it as dubious within Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Fue mencionado por Upchurch y colegas en 2004, quienes lo clasificaron como dudoso dentro de Sauropoda.

facts.statement: In 2007, Upchurch and colleagues published a detailed description of the dentary and teeth, declaring Chinshakiangosaurus a valid taxon.
facts.quote: En 2007, Upchurch y sus colegas publicaron una descripción exhaustiva del dentario y los dientes y declararon a Chinshakiangosaurus como un taxón válido.

facts.statement: Initially, Dong Zhiming classified Chinshakiangosaurus as a member of the Melanorosauridae, a group he thought consisted of prosauropods.
facts.quote: Inicialmente, Dong Zhiming clasificó a Chinshakiangosaurus como miembro de los Melanorosauridae, que él pensaba que era un grupo de prosaurópodos.

facts.statement: Dong Zhiming noted certain similarities between Chinshakiangosaurus and sauropods.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, ya notó ciertas semejanzas con los saurópodos.

facts.statement: Recent studies classify this genus as a very basal sauropod.
facts.quote: Estudios más recientes clasifican este género como un saurópodo muy basal.

facts.statement: The exact relationships of the genus remain unclear.
facts.quote: Las relaciones exactas no son claras, sin embargo.

facts.statement: The parent group of Chinshakiangosaurus is Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropoda

facts.statement: Chinshakiangosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Chinshakiangosaurus lived during the Hettangian stage, from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Hettangian (201.4 to 199.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Fengjiahe Formation, composed of mudstone, siltstone, and sandstone deposited by rivers and lakes.
facts.quote: Los fósiles fueron encontrados .

rejected.statement: The only known species, Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis, is known from a fragmentary skeleton found in Early Jurassic rocks in China.
rejected.quote: The only species, Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis, is known from a fragmentary skeleton found in Early Jurassic rocks in China.

rejected.statement: Chinshakiangosaurus is one of the few basal sauropods with preserved skull bones, suggesting early sauropods may have possessed fleshy cheeks.
rejected.quote: It is one of the few basal sauropods with preserved skull bones and therefore important for the understanding of the early evolution of this group, and also shows that early sauropods may have possessed fleshy cheeks.
